```{r}
library(tidycensus)
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(scales)

options(tigris_progress = FALSE)

data_file <- "race_edu_la_2021.rds"

if (file.exists(data_file)) {
  edu_race <- readRDS(data_file)
} else {
  race_vars <- c(
    "B15002A_001", "B15002A_015", "B15002A_031",  # White
    "B15002B_001", "B15002B_015", "B15002B_031",  # Black
    "B15002D_001", "B15002D_015", "B15002D_031",  # Asian
    "B15002I_001", "B15002I_015", "B15002I_031"   # Hispanic / Latino
  )
  
  raw <- get_acs(
    geography = "county",
    state     = "CA",
    county    = "Los Angeles",
    variables = race_vars,
    year      = 2021,
    survey    = "acs1",
    output    = "wide"
  ) %>%
    clean_names()
  
  edu_race <- tibble(
    race = c("White", "Black", "Asian", "Hispanic / Latino"),
    percent_bachelors = c(
      (raw$b15002a_015e + raw$b15002a_031e) / raw$b15002a_001e,
      (raw$b15002b_015e + raw$b15002b_031e) / raw$b15002b_001e,
      (raw$b15002d_015e + raw$b15002d_031e) / raw$b15002d_001e,
      (raw$b15002i_015e + raw$b15002i_031e) / raw$b15002i_001e
    ) * 100
  )
  
  saveRDS(edu_race, data_file)
}

ggplot(edu_race, aes(x = reorder(race, percent_bachelors), y = percent_bachelors, fill = race)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#1f78b4", "#33a02c", "#6a3a9a", "#e31a1c")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(scale = 1)) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Percentage with Bachelor's Degree",
    title = "Educational Attainment by Race",
    subtitle = "Percentage of Adults (25+) with a Bachelor's Degree or Higher in Los Angeles County (2021)",
    caption = "Source: U.S. Census Bureau, 2021 1-year ACS"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 20),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 14, margin = margin(b = 15)),
    axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```

This bar chart clearly illustrates the disparities in bachelor's degree attainment among major racial and ethnic groups in Los Angeles County. Asians have the highest percentage of adults with a bachelor’s degree, followed by Whites, Blacks, and Hispanic/Latino populations. These differences reflect complex social, economic, and historical factors shaping educational opportunities in the region. Understanding these patterns is crucial for policymakers and educators aiming to design targeted interventions that promote educational equity across all communities.
